audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRoot only serve sidecars for validated blocks?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The handler retrieves sidecars exclusively via `s.cfg.dataColumnStorage.Get(root, columns)` which returns `[]VerifiedRODataColumn`. The `VerifiedRODataColumn` type can only be constructed by the verification package after all requirements are satisfied. The secondary slot filter restricts by minReqSlot from FuluForkEpoch. No unvalidated code path exists.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No counterexample path found. The only source of data is `dataColumnStorage`, which only persists `VerifiedRODataColumn` items. The slot filter (`minReqSlot`) additionally restricts by time window. No attacker-controlled bypass exists to serve unvalidated data.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant holds: all served sidecars are `VerifiedRODataColumn` instances enforced by the type system at construction time. Secondary slot filter further restricts to `minReqSlot` derived from `FuluForkEpoch`.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: VerifiedRODataColumn type wrapper enforced by verification package; storage only accepts verified instances

audit_items.finding: Safe: The handler exclusively serves data from `dataColumnStorage` which only contains `VerifiedRODataColumn` instances. The type system and storage layer guarantee that only gossip-validated or RPC-verified sidecars are persisted and retrieved. The additional `minReqSlot` filter further restricts to the Fulu retention window.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-004: Are blobs from engine_getBlobsV2 correctly handled with trust assumption?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The function explicitly trusts the EL: 'We trust the execution layer we are connected to, so we can upgrade the read only data column sidecar into a verified one.' KZG cell proofs from `blobAndProofV2s.KzgProofs` are passed to `peerdas.ConstructDataColumnSidecars` but no explicit CL-side KZG verification is performed before calling `blocks.NewVerifiedRODataColumn`.
state_anomalies_found: No CL-side KZG verification of EL-sourced blobs before marking as VerifiedRODataColumn

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: If the EL returns malformed blobs with invalid cell proofs, `ConstructDataColumnSidecars` may produce structurally valid but cryptographically invalid sidecars marked `VerifiedRODataColumn` and broadcast without KZG verification. The security boundary is the JWT-authenticated EL connection. Downstream gossip peers independently perform KZG validation and will reject invalid columns.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: Compromised EL returns blobs with invalid cell proofs; these are stored and broadcast as 'verified' without CL-side KZG check. Downstream gossip peers reject them via independent KZG verification. Local node's reputation is degraded but no local state corruption occurs.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The Fulu spec permits trusting the local EL for blob reconstruction. The security impact is limited to the local node broadcasting invalid data; downstream validators enforce independent KZG checks. This is a deliberate architectural trust boundary, not a code vulnerability.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: JWT-authenticated EL connection; downstream gossip validators enforce independent KZG verification

audit_items.finding: The explicit EL trust assumption is spec-compliant for local reconstruction. The EL connection is authenticated via JWT, and any invalid data broadcast from this node will be independently rejected by gossip peers. The trust model is a deliberate architectural decision per the Fulu spec.
audit_items.recommendation: Consider adding CL-side KZG cell proof verification on EL-returned data as defense-in-depth, since `blobAndProofV2s.KzgProofs` are already available. This would prevent broadcasting invalid columns even if the EL is compromised or buggy.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005: Does the node enforce subscription checks before publishing data column sidecars?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: `BroadcastDataColumnSidecar` performs nil-check and fork digest lookup, then spawns a goroutine. No explicit custody/subscription check inside the function. Custody enforcement is at the call site (`broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars`) which only calls this for columns in `localNodeInfo.CustodyColumns` (computed by `peerdas.Info(nodeID, custodyGroupCount)`).

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: The function is only called from `broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars` for custody columns. No path exists where a non-custody column would be broadcast. Custody enforcement is at the caller layer.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Custody enforcement is at the call-site layer rather than inside `BroadcastDataColumnSidecar`. This is the same design pattern as `BroadcastAttestation` and `BroadcastBlob`. Current callers enforce custody correctly.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Caller (broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars) enforces custody column check before calling BroadcastDataColumnSidecar

audit_items.finding: Current design is compliant. The `BroadcastDataColumnSidecar` API is intentionally general-purpose (consistent with `BroadcastAttestation`, `BroadcastBlob`). Custody enforcement is the caller's responsibility, and all existing callers enforce it correctly via `localNodeInfo.CustodyColumns`.
audit_items.recommendation: As defense-in-depth, consider adding an optional custody assertion inside `BroadcastDataColumnSidecar` to protect against future incorrect callers.

audit_items.title: Can the anti-equivocation cache update be bypassed when sidecar publishing is skipped?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: `broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars` only iterates `localNodeInfo.CustodyColumns`. Non-custody columns are never added to `missingColumns`. `setSeenDataColumnIndex` is only called for custody columns after successful broadcast. Non-custody columns never have their seen-index set here by design.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: A reconstructed non-custody column arriving via gossip later would not be in `seenDataColumnCache` and would be processed normally. This is correct — the node is not responsible for non-custody columns. The gossip validator has its own deduplication path independent of reconstruction. No double-processing risk exists.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant holds: `setSeenDataColumnIndex` is correctly only called for successfully-broadcast custody columns. Gossip deduplication is independent and prevents double-processing regardless of reconstruction state.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Gossip validation layer independently tracks seen-status via seenDataColumnCache; reconstruction does not interfere

audit_items.finding: Correct by design. Custody columns are marked seen after broadcast; non-custody columns are not the node's responsibility and their absence from the seen-cache is intentional. The gossip deduplication mechanism operates independently and prevents any double-processing.

audit_items.title: Can imported data columns bypass gossip validation rules?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Reconstructed sidecars derive from `verifiedSidecars` which are `VerifiedRODataColumn` from local storage — already gossip-validated. `peerdas.ReconstructDataColumnSidecars` performs Reed-Solomon reconstruction over verified inputs. The `receiveDataColumn` path is intentionally skipped to avoid blocking concurrent gossip reception during the broadcast window.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Reconstruction inputs are always previously gossip-validated sidecars. Reed-Solomon reconstruction over valid inputs produces deterministic, mathematically guaranteed outputs. Re-validating reconstructed columns would be redundant given the cryptographic guarantees of the verified inputs. The skip of `receiveDataColumn` is documented and intentional.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Security invariant holds: reconstruction from N gossip-verified columns produces M verified columns where correctness follows from the KZG commitments embedded in the verified input sidecars. The skip of `receiveDataColumn` is a deliberate optimization documented in the code comment.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Inputs are VerifiedRODataColumn from storage; Reed-Solomon reconstruction is deterministic given valid inputs

audit_items.finding: Correct behavior. Reconstructed sidecars from gossip-verified inputs do not require re-validation. The intentional skip of `receiveDataColumn` is properly documented and serves the broadcast-before-seen-mark invariant, enabling concurrent gossip reception during the reconstruction window.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-009: Does BlobSidecarsByRange correctly handle deprecation?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The handler `blobSidecarsByRangeRPCHandler` contains no explicit check for Fulu fork activation. The wQuota is adjusted for ElectraForkEpoch but not deprecated for Fulu. `BlobRPCMinValidSlot` floors at `DenebForkEpoch` with no upper cap at `FuluForkEpoch`.
state_anomalies_found: No Fulu-era deprecation check for BlobSidecarsByRange handler

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: After Fulu activation, the handler continues accepting requests. Post-Fulu blocks have no blob sidecars, so actual data served is empty for post-Fulu slots. The handler silently returns nothing without indicating endpoint deprecation. No security impact since no sensitive data exists post-Fulu.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: Post-Fulu: peer requests BlobSidecarsByRange spanning the Fulu boundary. Handler serves pre-Fulu blobs and silently returns empty for post-Fulu slots without deprecation notification.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Per Fulu spec, BlobSidecarsByRange is deprecated post-Fulu. Implementation does not enforce this at the handler level. Practical impact is limited since post-Fulu blobs are absent from storage, but spec-correct behavior would explicitly indicate the transition.

audit_items.finding: Protocol compliance gap: `blobSidecarsByRangeRPCHandler` has no explicit Fulu deprecation check. Post-Fulu, no blob sidecars exist in storage, so the handler silently returns empty results. No security impact — blobs simply don't exist post-Fulu.
audit_items.recommendation: Add a Fulu activation check to explicitly cap the valid range at `FuluForkEpoch` in `BlobRPCMinValidSlot` or `blobSidecarsByRangeRPCHandler`, and optionally indicate endpoint deprecation post-Fulu activation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-009: Is BlobSidecarsByRange epoch range correctly enforced during Fulu transition?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: `BlobRPCMinValidSlot` computes minimum as `max(DenebForkEpoch, currEpoch - MinEpochsForBlobsSidecarsRequest)` with no upper bound cap at `FuluForkEpoch`. The retention window slides correctly but extends past Fulu territory where no blobs exist.
state_anomalies_found: No FuluForkEpoch upper cap in BlobRPCMinValidSlot

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: The lack of FuluForkEpoch cap does not cause incorrect serving — post-Fulu blobs don't exist. However, the absence means the spec constraint of serving blobs only in the [DenebForkEpoch, FuluForkEpoch] window is only implicitly enforced (no Fulu blobs) rather than explicitly enforced (code-level rejection).

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The spec requires blobs only served for the Deneb-to-Fulu window. Current implementation satisfies this implicitly but not explicitly. Protocol compliance gap rather than security vulnerability.

audit_items.finding: Protocol compliance gap: `BlobRPCMinValidSlot` lacks an explicit cap at `FuluForkEpoch`. The Fulu spec constrains the blob retention window to `[max(DenebForkEpoch, currEpoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS), FuluForkEpoch]`. Only the lower bound is explicitly enforced; the upper bound is implicit (no Fulu blobs exist). No security impact in practice.
audit_items.recommendation: Add explicit upper cap: `if params.FuluEnabled() && minStart > params.BeaconConfig().FuluForkEpoch { minStart = params.BeaconConfig().FuluForkEpoch }` in `BlobRPCMinValidSlot` to make the Fulu boundary explicit and spec-compliant.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-009: Are peers NOT penalized for transition-period blob requests?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Peers are downscored only when `validateBlobsByRange` returns an error. `validateBlobsByRange` clamps ranges rather than rejecting them — `start < minStartSlot` is silently adjusted, `start > current` returns noop range. Errors only occur for overflow conditions, count=0, or `start > maxStart` (2x maxRequest).

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Peers legitimately syncing across the Deneb/Fulu transition will NOT be penalized — `validateBlobsByRange` returns errors only for genuinely malformed requests (overflow, zero count, wildly out-of-range start). The clamping behavior prevents false penalization.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant holds: transition-period requests within a valid range are not penalized. Clamping logic in `validateBlobsByRange` handles edge cases without triggering false penalization.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: validateBlobsByRange clamps ranges; downscoring only on genuine protocol errors (overflow, count=0, wildly-out-of-range start)

audit_items.finding: Safe: Transition-period blob requests are handled gracefully via range clamping. Peers are only penalized for genuinely malformed requests. The clamping approach (silently adjusting out-of-range boundaries) prevents false penalization during the Deneb-to-Fulu transition.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Is ENR eth2 value correctly encoded as exactly 16 bytes?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: In `forkEntry`, `sszEncodedForkEntry` is initialized as `make([]byte, 16)` (exactly 16 bytes). `ENRForkID` SSZ encoding: 4 bytes CurrentForkDigest + 4 bytes NextForkVersion + 8 bytes NextForkEpoch = 16 bytes total. In `updateENR`, `enrForkID.MarshalSSZ()` produces deterministically 16 bytes.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: 16-byte invariant is maintained: writing uses `MarshalSSZ()` (deterministic 16 bytes); reading pre-allocates 16 bytes and passes pointer to `record.Load`. Any ENR with non-16-byte eth2 entry fails `UnmarshalSSZ` and is rejected.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: 16-byte invariant proven: SSZ layout of ENRForkID is fixed-size (4+4+8=16 bytes). Both encoding and decoding enforce this. Malformed external ENR entries fail parsing and are correctly rejected.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: ENRForkID SSZ fixed-size encoding; 16-byte pre-allocation in forkEntry; UnmarshalSSZ validation

audit_items.finding: Safe: ENR eth2 encoding is correctly maintained at exactly 16 bytes. The SSZ fixed-size layout enforces this at the type level. Malformed entries from external peers fail `UnmarshalSSZ` and are correctly rejected by `compareForkENR`.

audit_items.title: Can ENR no-fork invariant be violated?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: In `updateENR`, when `entry.Epoch == next.Epoch` (no upcoming fork), `NextForkEpoch` is set to `FarFutureEpoch`. The `nfd` entry is set to zero bytes when `entry.ForkDigest == next.ForkDigest`, correctly signaling no upcoming different fork.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: The no-fork invariant (NextForkEpoch = FarFutureEpoch when no next fork) is correctly enforced. nfd entry uses zero bytes when current and next digests match. forkWatcher's zero-initialization of `scheduleEntry` means first slot tick always triggers initial ENR update.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant holds. The `FarFutureEpoch` sentinel is correctly set via `entry.Epoch == next.Epoch` check. Zero nfd bytes correctly signal no upcoming different fork digest.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: entry.Epoch == next.Epoch check sets FarFutureEpoch; zero nfd bytes when digests match

audit_items.finding: Safe: The ENR no-fork invariant is correctly implemented. `FarFutureEpoch` sentinel is properly set when no upcoming fork is scheduled, and `nfd` correctly uses zero bytes in the no-fork state.

audit_items.title: Can ENR epoch be manipulated to reflect sync state instead of wall-clock time?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The forkWatcher uses `slots.NewSlotTicker(s.genesisTime, SecondsPerSlot)` — wall-clock based. ENR reflects wall-clock fork schedule, not chain sync state. ENR update triggered when ForkDigest changes (fork transition detected by wall clock).

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: ENR epoch reflects the node's wall-clock fork schedule, not sync position. This is correct per spec: ENR should advertise the intended fork at given wall-clock time. A syncing node with correct wall-clock correctly advertises the target fork, enabling proper peer discovery.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Wall-clock-based ENR updates are intentional and spec-correct. Using sync state would be incorrect — it would break peering for syncing nodes by advertising an outdated fork.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: slotTicker wall-clock based via genesisTime; ENR reflects intended fork schedule, not sync state

audit_items.finding: Safe: Wall-clock-based ENR updates are spec-correct. The ENR advertises fork schedule compatibility (intended fork), not sync progress. This is the correct design — syncing nodes should advertise their target fork to enable proper peer discovery and syncing.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001/tb-002: Can a malicious peer forge a data column sidecar with a valid BLS proposer signature?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: `ValidProposerSignature` calls `dv.sc.VerifySignature(signatureData, parentState)` performing full BLS12-381 verification against the proposer's public key from `parentState`. `SidecarProposerExpected` independently verifies ProposerIndex matches computed proposer for (slot, parentRoot).

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Forging a valid BLS12-381 signature requires knowledge of the proposer's private key (~128-bit security level). The dual-check (BLS + shuffling) requires bypassing two independent security mechanisms simultaneously. No feasible attack path exists.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Authentication invariant holds with cryptographic security. BLS12-381 provides computationally-unforgeable authentication. Signature cache provides additional replay protection and performance optimization.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: BLS12-381 signature verification against proposer pubkey from beacon state; signature cache for deduplication

audit_items.finding: Safe: BLS12-381 signature forgery is computationally infeasible. The implementation correctly retrieves the proposer's public key from the parent beacon state and performs full BLS signature verification. The signature cache provides replay protection.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Is three-layer integrity verification enforced for all sidecars?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Three integrity layers are in `GossipDataColumnSidecarRequirements`: (1) BLS proposer signature (`RequireValidProposerSignature`), (2) Merkle inclusion proof (`RequireSidecarInclusionProven`), (3) KZG cell proof (`RequireSidecarKzgProofVerified`). All must be satisfied before `VerifiedRODataColumns()` returns.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: `results.allSatisfied()` verifies all requirements are satisfied. No path exists to skip requirements without `SatisfyRequirement()`, which is only used for forkchoice-dependent checks during batch sync. For gossip, all three integrity layers are enforced.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: All three integrity layers enforced for gossip. RPC paths omit BLS signature per spec (RPC serves previously gossip-validated data). `results.allSatisfied()` prevents any requirement from being silently bypassed.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: results.allSatisfied() enforces all requirements; GossipDataColumnSidecarRequirements includes all three integrity checks

audit_items.finding: Safe: Three-layer integrity verification (BLS signature + Merkle inclusion + KZG cell proof) is fully enforced for gossip-received sidecars via `GossipDataColumnSidecarRequirements`. The RPC path omission of BLS signature is spec-correct. The `results.allSatisfied()` framework ensures no requirement can be silently bypassed.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Is gossip validation ordered from cheapest to most expensive?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: `ValidProposerSignature` (expensive BLS, step 7) runs before `SidecarParentSlotLower` (cheap forkchoice `fc.Slot()`, step 8) and `SidecarDescendsFromFinalized` (cheap forkchoice `fc.HasNode()`, step 9). The code explicitly acknowledges this spec deviation. However, steps 8-9 only need forkchoice data (available after step 5), NOT the parent state needed by ValidProposerSignature. Steps 8-9 can be moved before step 7 without breaking dependencies.
state_anomalies_found: ValidProposerSignature (BLS, expensive) runs before SidecarParentSlotLower (fc.Slot only, cheap) and SidecarDescendsFromFinalized (fc.HasNode only, cheap)
Steps 8-9 only require forkchoice which is available after step 5 (SidecarParentSeen), not parent state needed by BLS

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: The ordering deviation is real: steps 8-9 (`SidecarParentSlotLower`, `SidecarDescendsFromFinalized`) only call `dv.fc.Slot(parentRoot)` and `dv.fc.HasNode(parentRoot)` — forkchoice-only operations NOT requiring parent state. They could be moved before `ValidProposerSignature` (step 7). An attacker with a valid proposer key could craft sidecars that pass BLS but fail step 8 or 9, causing unnecessary BLS computation. The BLS signature cache mitigates repeated-signature attacks from the same proposer.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: Attacker with a valid proposer key crafts sidecar with correct BLS signature but invalid parent-slot relationship. Current: BLS runs (expensive) then SidecarParentSlotLower fails (cheap). Optimal: SidecarParentSlotLower fails first (cheap), BLS never runs. Practical exploitability: LOW — requires possession of a valid proposer key.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The ordering deviation is partially justified by BLS's dependency on parent state. However, steps 8-9 do NOT share this dependency and could be moved before BLS. The BLS signature cache reduces practical DoS risk for repeated signatures. The deviation is a spec compliance gap for DoS hardening.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: BLS signature cache provides protection against repeated identical signatures from the same proposer

audit_items.finding: Spec deviation in gossip validation ordering: `ValidProposerSignature` (expensive BLS) runs at step 7 before `SidecarParentSlotLower` (step 8) and `SidecarDescendsFromFinalized` (step 9), which are cheap forkchoice lookups using only `dv.fc.Slot()` and `dv.fc.HasNode()` — operations available after `SidecarParentSeen` (step 5) and NOT requiring parent state. The code comment justifies the placement by 'dependency on parent root' but this only applies to the BLS check itself, not to steps 8-9. While exploiting this requires an attacker to possess a valid proposer key (making practical exploitation very difficult), it represents a DoS hardening gap. The BLS signature cache mitigates repeated-signature attacks.
audit_items.recommendation: Move `SidecarParentSlotLower()` (forkchoice only: `dv.fc.Slot(parentRoot)`) and `SidecarDescendsFromFinalized()` (forkchoice only: `dv.fc.HasNode(parentRoot)`) to before `ValidProposerSignature()`. Both only need forkchoice data available after step 5. The new order would be: ...[5] SidecarParentSeen, [6] SidecarParentValid, [7] SidecarParentSlotLower, [8] SidecarDescendsFromFinalized, [9] ValidProposerSignature [BLS], [10] SidecarInclusionProven, [11] KZG, [12] SidecarProposerExpected.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Can a non-proposer node get a sidecar accepted by claiming proposer identity?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Two independent checks prevent identity impersonation: (1) `SidecarProposerExpected` verifies `ProposerIndex` against shuffling-computed proposer for (slot, parentRoot), (2) `ValidProposerSignature` verifies BLS signature is from the claimed `ProposerIndex`'s key from beacon state. Both must pass independently.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Attacker must: (a) set correct ProposerIndex (knowable from shuffling, but harmless), AND (b) produce valid BLS signature from that proposer's private key (computationally infeasible). Setting wrong ProposerIndex fails SidecarProposerExpected. Setting correct ProposerIndex but signing with own key fails ValidProposerSignature. Both guards must be bypassed simultaneously.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Identity verification invariant is cryptographically sound. BLS signature verification + computed proposer check provides complete protection against identity impersonation. Both guards must be bypassed simultaneously, requiring the proposer's private key.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: SidecarProposerExpected (shuffling-based proposer check) + ValidProposerSignature (BLS against beacon state pubkey) as two independent identity guards

audit_items.finding: Safe: Two independent and complementary identity guards prevent proposer impersonation. `SidecarProposerExpected` checks ProposerIndex against RANDAO shuffling; `ValidProposerSignature` verifies BLS signature against the proposer's beacon state public key. Both must be bypassed simultaneously — computationally infeasible without the proposer's private key.
